causal_test: Exact Dukascopy entry-at-proof replay. 017 high-confidence actions remain at signal; low-confidence/abstained candidates are delayed to actual first-touch proof tick. All entries merge chronologically in one-position ledger. No signal-time credit after observing proof.
april_selection: No candidate met simultaneous requirements of less gross loss, >=98% winner retention, non-worse net and <=0.5pp success degradation.

winner_recovery_example.interpretation: Proof can recover many winners, but it reopens too much loss and worsens economics.

pullback_reaccel_screen.interpretation: Proof->micro-pullback->reacceleration also fails to preserve 017 economics.

main_diagnosis: The July first-touch correlation is real as an ownership signal, but confirmation occurs after too much of the short-horizon excursion has already been spent. This is a confirmation-tax/latency problem, not a lack of correlation. Delayed proof is therefore unsuitable as the primary HFT entry trigger under the current spread/lifecycle geometry.
integration_lesson: Use dynamic proof information as state/lifecycle context only if it arrives after entry; for better ownership before entry, move research toward leading raw-tick microstructure: signed tick imbalance, tick-arrival acceleration, extreme-renewal asymmetry, quote-gap/spread state, entropy/sequence structure, intrinsic-event clocks, and execution stability.
community_cross_reference: MQL5 Microstructure Part 5: true microstructure is tick-level; bar aggregation erases spread/order-flow information.
MQL5 Microstructure Part 6: order-flow direction and confidence should be conditioned on noise and volatility.
MQL5 Microstructure Parts 7/8: separate regime label, confidence and directional response; adaptive thresholds can suppress stressed/noisy signals.
MQL5 Dynamic Multi-Pair Part 9: spread expansion, tick velocity, quote gaps, micro-volatility and execution stability should be separate execution-quality states.

MQL5 ORB/adaptive channel work: pending/confirmed/expired breakout states and retest confirmation are reconstructible, but our exact-tick replay shows confirmation lag is too expensive for this HFT path.
Directional-change intrinsic-time literature supports event-based clocks and overshoot state; candidate for earlier ownership features rather than delayed entry.
Hobbyist breakout discussions repeatedly warn that thin breakout edges can be consumed by fees/slippage and excessive confirmation.
forward_integrity: May-Jun remain numerically untouched by proof-family selection. July informed mechanism-family design through 017A and is therefore a stress-validation month, not a pristine mechanism-selection holdout for 018. August remains sealed.
